rationale: This is the archive's Clean Working-Capital Margin with the only change being the MA/VOL window shortened from 5 to 3 — a purely cosmetic parameter tweak of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantive mechanism change.

Replacing the unstable small-denominator ratio with a rank-space conjunctive MIN is a defensible functional-form repair that is internally consistent (both components are "good" states, so positive sign is correct), though it recycles the same two ingredients as the prior weak signal and is only marginally novel.

This is the archived Leveraged Opaque-Accrual Penalty with MIN flipped to MAX on identical inputs — a single-operator variant whose long leg collapses toward low-leverage, low-accrual firms and therefore largely re-tests the well-known leverage/accrual quality effects rather than a new interaction.

Inventory growth measured against realized throughput is essentially the published Abarbanell–Bushee inventory-versus-sales fundamental signal and the Thomas–Zhang inventory-change anomaly, so the trend-window wrapper does not make it a genuinely new cross-theme mechanism.

Subtracting raw trends of two ratios with wildly different scales (gross margin bounded near [0,1] versus wcap/sale, which is unbounded and sign-unstable) means the composite will be dominated by the working-capital-intensity trend, reducing it to a noisy proxy for the known working-capital-accrual/NOA-growth anomaly rather than the stated margin-versus-capital comparison.

The conjunctive design is internally consistent, the two trend components are commensurably scaled by assets, and requiring debt-financing-adjusted cash confirmation of retained-earnings growth is a substantively different test from the prior MAX-based "corroboration" gap, though it overlaps partly with known external-financing anomalies.
